options_evaluated: Glass-fiber reinforced polyamide (PA6-GF30) overmolded with TPU elastomer
Monomaterial post-consumer recycled (PCR) ABS with mechanical fasteners
Bio-based PLA housing with glued joints
assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial post-consumer recycled (PCR) ABS with mechanical fasteners and no overmolded elastomer grips.
assessments.rationale: Overmolded elastomer grips (like TPU on PA6) cannot be easily separated, severely reducing the ease and quality of recycling (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d)) and leading to downcycling or incineration. Monomaterial PCR-ABS allows high-purity polymer recovery. Avoiding overmolding also prevents the generation of mixed-material microplastics during mechanical shredding processes (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (p)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: User Experience/Ergonomics (TPU overmolding provides superior grip and vibration dampening) and Manufacturing (monomaterial mechanical assembly may require more parts and complex mold designs).

options_evaluated: Threaded fasteners (standard Torx screws) with threaded brass inserts
assessments.recommendation: Threaded fasteners (standard Torx screws) with threaded brass inserts
assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners allow non-destructive disassembly, which is essential for the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c)). It avoids solutions detrimental to recycling (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e)) by allowing easy separation of plastics, metals, and electronics, thereby reducing the amount of waste generated in end-of-life treatment (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (r)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (ultrasonic welding and adhesives are faster and cheaper to assemble in mass production) and Physical Durability (welded joints can offer better dust and water resistance).

options_evaluated: Brushed DC motor with integrated gearbox
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets
Coreless motor with permanently bonded rotor assembly
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets
assessments.rationale: Brushless motors have a significantly longer service life, supporting product longevity and remanufacturing (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c)). Designing the motor for easy extraction of the rotor allows high-quality recycling of critical raw materials like neodymium magnets (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d)), avoiding solutions that lock valuable materials into unsorted scrap (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Sourcing and Cost (brushless motors and rare-earth magnets increase initial bill of materials cost compared to cheap brushed motors).

options_evaluated: Passive aluminum heatsinks mechanically secured with ventilation slots
Phase change materials (PCM) integrated into the housing
assessments.recommendation: Passive aluminum heatsinks mechanically secured with ventilation slots
assessments.rationale: Potting compounds completely encapsulate electronic components, making repair, component harvesting, or recycling impossible (violating ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c) and (d)). Mechanical heatsinks can be easily detached and recycled as high-grade aluminum, reducing the environmental footprint and waste generated in end-of-life treatment (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (m), (r)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Reliability/Environmental Protection (potting compounds protect electronics from moisture, dust, and vibration, extending use-phase life in harsh environments).

options_evaluated: Integrated single-board design with soldered battery and motor connections
Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors for battery, switch, PCB, and motor
Semi-modular design with soldered wire interconnects
assessments.recommendation: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors for battery, switch, PCB, and motor
assessments.rationale: A fully modular architecture allows individual components to be replaced or upgraded, directly facilitating ease of repair, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c)). It prevents the premature disposal of the entire tool due to a single component failure (e.g., a broken switch), thereby minimizing waste generation (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (r)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing and Space Optimization (plug-and-play connectors increase assembly complexity, component cost, and require more internal physical space, making the tool bulkier).

options_evaluated: Standardized, tool-free removable and shareable slide-on battery pack
assessments.recommendation: Standardized, tool-free removable and shareable slide-on battery pack
assessments.rationale: Integrated batteries lead to early product disposal once the battery degrades (violating ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (c)). A removable battery pack extends product life and allows safe, high-quality recycling of lithium-ion cells (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (d)). It also avoids severe safety hazards (thermal runaway) and resource loss during shredding at end-of-life (ESPR 2024/1781 Annex I (e), (g)).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Industrial Design and Ergonomics (integrated batteries allow for a much sleeker, lighter, and more balanced tool design).
